one_month_reasoning: Micron does not report before 1 Nov (FQ1 FY27 is mid/late Dec). In the window are Samsung Q3 prelim (~7-8 Oct) and full results (~29-30 Oct), SK hynix Q3 (27 or 28 Oct), Kioxia (~30 Oct), Korea 1-20 Oct exports (~21 Oct), FOMC (27-28 Oct) and hyperscaler 2027 capex guides. Peer prints should confirm tight contract supply (TrendForce 4Q26 DRAM +10-15%). Two things I under-weighted in round 1 lean the other way. (1) The Micron Taiwan strike vote (early Oct) and Taichung mediation (22 Oct) are confirmed by independent press; that is a negative-skew headline that could also be read as a supply disruption. (2) TrendForce spot data for mid/late Sep show DDR5 demand cooling, DDR4 2Gx8 correcting and NAND wafer prices slipping, an early second-derivative signal that peer calls may be asked about. I drop the round-1 post-earnings drift (MU moved only +0.9% on its beat). The model is 90% lognormal centred at $1,080 with sigma 20% (a little under 80%/3.5 because Micron's own event has passed) plus 10% weight on a strike or second-derivative selloff centred at $960. That puts P(>= spot) at 0.49.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (FY28 EPS $195 x 5.1x = $995, 40%), NTM EV/EBITDA (FY28 EBITDA $245B x 4.0x + ~$190B horizon net cash over 1.15B shares = $1,017, 30%) and a cycle-aware DCF at Oct-2027 (FCF $174B/$105B/$70B/$85B for FY28-31, 3% terminal growth on $80B mid-cycle FCF, 11% discount rate, + $190B net cash = $1,059, 30%), which gives about $1,021, ~5% below spot.

inputs_detail.derivation: Kept ~5% below FY28 consensus, against the supervisor's ~$200. FY28 runs Sep-27 to Aug-28, so about two-thirds falls in CY28. BofA (two secondary reports, Aug and Sep 2026) sees 2028 DRAM ASP down ~5-10% and NAND ~14% from 2027 peaks. TrendForce spot data show early softening, and FY28 consensus already assumes +17% EPS growth over FY27. The FQ1 guide beat (8-K) lifts FY27 more than FY28, so I leave FY28 here.

Core memory peers (SK hynix 4.65x, Samsung 4.73x, Kioxia ~4.2x, Nanya 5.4x, Sandisk 7.8x) restated to NTM have a median of 4.7x; MU is at ~6.0x. I accept the supervisor's finding that SK hynix and Samsung also hold long-term contracts, so the SCA floor justifies less than the 17% premium I used. I use ~8%: below the supervisor's 5.2x cap because by Oct-2027 the market will be pricing the 2028 supply wave (Yongin equipment Feb-27, M15X 80k wpm in 2027, ID1 and Tongluo mid-27).

methods.inputs: FY28 EBITDA ~$245B x 4.0x NTM = $980B EV + ~$190B net cash at Oct-2027, / 1.15B diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FQ4 non-GAAP operating margin 82.3% plus D&A, less margin give-back as 2028 ASPs ease (BofA) and opex rises.

Core-peer NTM EV/EBITDA (StockAnalysis EV over NTM EBITDA scaled from TTM by the trailing/forward P/E ratio): SK hynix ~5.2x, Samsung ~2.5x, Sandisk ~6.5x, Kioxia ~3.0x, Nanya ~3.5x; median ~3.5-4.0x. MU is ~4.6x today. 4.0x sits at the core median, replacing round-1's 3.5x, which I had derived from P/E rather than EV data.

$68.3B net cash less $12.7B refundable SCA deposits = $55.6B. Add FY27 FCF of ~$135-145B: consensus NI ~$203B ($176.42 x 1.15B) + ~$12B D&A - capex ~$60B (>$50B guided, 2H higher) - ~$10-15B working capital on revenue growing from $54B to $70B+ a quarter. Buybacks are value-neutral. This is up from my round-1 $160B, which the supervisor rightly called too low, and a bit under its $200B because it ignored working capital and capex overrun.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued at Oct-2027: FCF FY28 $174B, FY29 $105B, FY30 $70B, FY31 $85B; terminal $80B x 1.03 / (11% - 3%) = $1,030B; 11% discount rate; EV $1,028B + $190B net cash, / 1.15B

inputs_detail.derivation: Cycle turn as 2028 supply arrives: BofA 2028 DRAM -8%/NAND -14%, CXMT to 420k+ wpm, SK hynix Yongin from Feb-27 plus M15X, Samsung P5 mass production late 2028. FY30 is the trough. Management says margins at SCA floor prices stay 'meaningfully above any prior cycle peak', so the trough FCF stays positive and large.
About 1.3x FY26 adj. FCF of $62.3B, reflecting a revenue base that is roughly three times larger and floor-priced contracts through 2030. 3% is long-run nominal growth.
Effectively all-equity (net cash, BBB+ rated per prepared remarks), but with very high cyclicality and 80% realized volatility, so a cost of equity above a typical large-cap 9%.
As in the EV/EBITDA leg; one horizon basis across all methods (fixes the round-1 mismatch flagged by the supervisor).

bear.story: Dated supply additions bunch up in 2027: SK hynix M15X to ~80k wpm and Yongin tools from Feb-27, Micron ID1 and Tongluo mid-27, CXMT toward 420k wpm, and Samsung P5 shell done 1H27. Spot softening (TrendForce Sep) spreads to contract by mid-2027, and the market discounts BofA's 2028 decline as something worse. FY28 EPS expectations fall toward $140-150 and MU trades at ~4x like 2018, partly cushioned by ~$165/sh of cash.

base.story: Contract supply stays tight through 2027 (TrendForce 4Q26 +10-15%, HBM ASP +121% in 2027; SK hynix 'worst supply year'). FY27 EPS lands near or above $180. At the horizon the market prices FY28 EPS of ~$195-205 at ~5x, near a perceived peak, plus a growing cash pile and higher buybacks from Dec-2026.

bull.story: SCA floors and HBM resets make the cycle look structurally longer. BofA-style 'soft landing' is pushed to 2029, consensus moves toward $250+, and the multiple holds ~6-7x on contracted floors and $190B+ net cash.

comps_summary.peer_range: Core DRAM/NAND manufacturers, NTM basis: P/E 4.2x (Kioxia) to 7.8x (Sandisk), median 4.7x; EV/EBITDA ~2.5x (Samsung) to ~6.5x (Sandisk), median ~3.5-4.0x. Their 20-24x P/Es and the trailing EV/EBITDA figures (13.95x median, round 1) must not be read as forward. Only five genuine DRAM/NAND manufacturers are listed.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.1x NTM P/E is ~8% above the 4.7x core median, inside the 4.2-7.8x range, and below MU's ~6.0x today. 4.0x NTM EV/EBITDA is at the core median and below MU's ~4.6x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: There are two persistent sources of a small premium. (1) About $150B of floor-priced RPO and $32B of customer commitments ($12.7B deposits), covering >35% of revenue through 2030. Its value is partly shared with SK hynix and Samsung, who also hold long-term HBM contracts, so it is worth less than I assumed in round 1. (2) US listing and capital return without the Korea governance discount. Against these, Samsung's KRW168T net cash weakens the balance-sheet argument, and by Oct-2027 the 2028 supply wave will weigh on all memory multiples. So ~8%, not 17%. No sell-side outperformance call is used.

thesis_break_reason: Rebuilt from post-print numbers rather than carried over. Today's net cash ex-deposits is ~$48/sh, so $600 values the operating business at ~$550/sh, or ~3.1x FY27 consensus EPS ($176) when FQ1 alone is guided at $38 with sequential growth. By Oct-2027 it would be ~$435/sh ex-cash on ~$165/sh of cash, ~2.2x FY28 consensus. A price that low would mean the market expects FY28 EPS of ~$135 or less, a 30%+ cut and far worse than BofA's 'healthy correction' (2028 DRAM -8%). That needs a real turn: TrendForce contract prices flat or down, spot softening spreading from DDR4/DDR5 into contract, hyperscaler capex cuts, SCA floor renegotiation, or a prolonged Taiwan strike that hits output. It coincides with my bear-case price.

reasoning: Round 2 takes in the supervisor's corrections and adds a few more industry checks. Accepted: horizon net cash was too low, rebuilt to ~$190B (~$165/sh) from FY27 consensus less capex and working capital, against the supervisor's $200B. Peer EV/EBITDA is restated to NTM (core median ~4.0x, not the 13.95x trailing figure). The peer set for multiples is narrowed to five DRAM/NAND makers (NTM P/E median 4.7x). The 17% P/E premium is cut to ~8% (5.1x). The normalized method, which mixed today's cash with horizon values, is replaced by a cycle-aware DCF on one horizon basis. Not fully accepted: the supervisor's lift of FY28 EPS to ~$200. FY28 is mostly CY28, where BofA (secondary reports, Aug/Sep) sees DRAM -8% and NAND -14%, and TrendForce spot updates (16 and 23 Sep) already show softening, so I keep $195. New industry evidence on dated supply: SK hynix Yongin tools from Feb-27, M15X ~80k wpm in 2027, Samsung P5 mass production late 2028. These keep the bear case anchored to mid-2027 to 2028 supply additions. Methods give $995 / $1,017 / $1,059, blended to ~$1,021, ~5% below spot. The ladder is a three-lognormal mix: bear $600 (27%, sigma 37%), base $1,060 (48%, 22%), bull $1,750 (25%, 25%). The mean is ~$1,108 and the median ~$1,050, so P(>= spot) is 0.49 and P(< $537) ~10%. Effective volatility is ~55-65%, below the trailing 80% inflated by the +490% run. Research was limited to ~8 follow-up searches and fetches. The BofA view is still only from secondary reports (itiger, Kaohoon); I could not reach the original note, so it is labelled secondary and only trims EPS. The SK hynix fab timing comes from a search summary of a Reuters story.
